title: CQRS, Projections & Event Sourcing
summary: Separate strongly consistent write models from denormalized read views, and know when immutable event logs pay off.
body:
`CQRS` (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) and `Event Sourcing` solve different problems and should not be conflated. Most systems that benefit from read/write separation need `CQRS` with outbox/CDC projections, not full event sourcing.

## CQRS without event sourcing
Keep a normalized transactional store on the write path to enforce invariants, and project asynchronous read models tailored to query patterns:
- Write model: normalized relational rows enforcing uniqueness, version checks, and authorization.
- Read projections: Elasticsearch documents for faceted search, Redis sorted sets for leaderboards/feeds, or pre-joined board views.
- Explicitly handle read-your-own-writes lag: return the mutated entity directly from the command response, pass a causal `min_version` token, or merge recent client mutations until the projection catches up.

## When Event Sourcing is justified
Store immutable domain events `(stream_id, version, event_type, payload)` as the primary source of truth only when auditability, temporal replay, or balanced accounting is a core requirement (financial ledgers, compliance audit trails, collaborative operation logs):
- Enforce optimistic concurrency on append with a unique `(stream_id, expected_version)` constraint.
- Bound aggregate load time with periodic state snapshots every `N` events so hydration reads `latest_snapshot + tail_events`.
- Never fire external side effects (emails, card charges, webhooks) directly from replayable projection handlers.

## Operational pitfalls
- Schema evolution is permanent: immutable events require additive schemas or explicit upcasters across historical versions.
- Regulatory deletion (`GDPR` right-to-erasure) conflicts with immutable logs: keep PII out of raw event payloads or encrypt per-subject fields with erasable keys (crypto-shredding).
